title: Is a shape with four equal sides and one right angle a square?
description: A shape with four equal sides is a rhombus, and so a parallelogram. The neighbours of the right angle are one hundred eighty minus ninety, and the opposite angle is equal, so all four angles are right angles. The angles are added to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: in a parallelogram, neighbouring angles add up to one hundred eighty degrees, so one right angle forces the other three. Watch for students who think the other corners can lean.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 8)
video_script.why: The child uses the family rules, as in the solved example, to show that four equal sides and one right angle force a square.
video_script.substitution: the book's question of a four-sided shape with four equal sides and one angle of 90 degrees
video_script.anchor: a four-sided shape with four equal sides and one marked right angle
never_show: a leaning corner drawn as a right angle
maths_rules: four equal sides make a rhombus, and a rhombus is a parallelogram
neighbouring angles of a parallelogram add up to 180, so each neighbour of the 90 degree angle is 180 - 90 = 90
opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so the last angle is 90 too
four equal sides and four right angles make a square
video_script.design: One idea: neighbouring angles of a parallelogram add up to 180, so one right angle forces the rest. One shape stays on the board and each angle is marked as it is found.
open_questions: The book asks for construction and measurement too; the video gives the reasoning and names the diagonal check without a measured length.
